event_description: This special event is designed to spark curiosity and deepen appreciation for our desert environment through hands-on activities, interactive learning experiences and performances, led by local organizations dedicated to sharing the wonders of the Sonoran Desert. Guests will have the chance to explore desert plants and wildlife, discover cultural traditions, and engage in educational fun for all ages. As part of the celebration, the Museum is offering pay-what-you-wish admission all day, ensuring that all families can enjoy the event as well as the exhibits inside the Museum. In addition to immersive activities, attendees can enjoy food from local food trucks Ensenada Street Food and Reservation Sensation. Desert Discovery Day partners include Academy of Math and Science Prince, Arizona Department of Environmental Quality, Cooper Center for Environmental Learning, Flandrau Science Center. There will also be performances by Ballet Folklorico del Desierto and Mariachi Arizona, plus traditional Tohono O’odham Waila music by Gertie and the T.O. Boyz. During the event, at about 11 am, the Museum will unveil its new Tree of Life mural, an art installation by Jeff Christensen and Maggie Mae Mosaics that honors the Museum’s 40th Anniversary. Desert Discovery Day is supported by Arizona Complete Health, Bayer, Pima County Office of Tourism, Tucson Electric Power, Tucson Medical Center and Renewal by Anderson.

event_description: Join us for Free Discovery Nights from 5-7 pm every Thursday at Children’s Museum Tucson! Discovery Nights are part of CMT’s collaborative Aprendemos bilingual program. Discovery Nights provide flexibility for working families and offer inclusive hands-on exploration in arts and science activities. Discovery Nights programming includes an interactive blend of science and arts. Discovery Nights include bilingual activities in an evening program providing flexibility for working caregivers to experience the Museum for free admission. Activities include bilingual Storytime, interactive pop-up science experiments like cloud in a bottle, ooblek, catapults or robot hands; and arts projects like nebula spin art, pumpkin playdough, or sound sandwich. CMT’s exhibits are fully accessible and provide the backdrop for creative exploration. Thank you to our Discovery Night sponsors. The generous partnership of Institute of Museum and Library Services, Pima County and Southwestern Foundation for Education and Historical Preservation makes Discovery Nights free for everyone! SOUTHWESTERN FOUNDATION FOR EDUCATION AND HISTORICAL PRESERVATION

event_description: The Nature Niños open arts & craft activity opens at 10 am and is available until CMOV closure. This activity is related to the story time book of the day and is nature-focused. The indoor space includes exhibits from the original Oro Valley location: Airways, Peek-a-Boo Place, Farmers Market, Fun Mirrors and the Light Table. This area is still designed for kids 5 and younger. The indoor space is open 9 am-1 pm Tuesdays-Sundays. Outdoor spaces have activities and exhibits that older kids will definitely enjoy: Block Building; Clay Studio; Mud Kitchen; Water Table; Paint Sculpture; an outside Art Studio with painting, drawing and even pretend planting; outdoor musical instruments; the Meditation Garden is also within the CMOV space, with music and slate painting. These spaces will be accessible whenever Tohono Chul is open.
